edits.description: A parent describes once how the family does something (party plan, ski-trip packing, school-form explainer); Tony turns it into a named skill, and after the next deploy Happy loads it whenever a request matches the skill's one-line description. A skill goes live only after Tony has read it.
caveats: Asking Happy to save a skill from iMessage does not work on this stack by default: sandboxed runs do not construct the `skill_workshop` tool even when it is allowlisted, so `/learn` cannot stage a draft. The M1 doctor baseline in the config repo already shows this warning for every agent. The documented exception is a human turn with host-granted library-authoring authority, and personal-library authoring publishes with no pending draft, which would skip Tony's review. That is one more reason to keep `skill_workshop` off every family agent's allowlist.
A skill is know-how. It cannot add tools or accounts, so "learn to order the groceries" still ends at a list.
A skill is instruction text loaded into future sessions. One written from a pasted web page or an email is a stored injection, so author only from the parent's own words.
No marketplace skills: an audit reported by The Hacker News found 341 malicious entries among 2,857 ClawHub skills in early 2026.
Turnaround is "when Tony next deploys", not instant.
A new or changed workspace skill is picked up on the next turn after the skills watcher sees the file change, or after the gateway restart that a deploy performs. No /new is needed.

Happy does not run a skill automatically every time: the prompt lists only each skill's name and one-line description, and the model reads the full text when it judges the request relevant, so that line has to be precise. Calling the skill by name (`/skill <name>`) is the sure route, where that command is accepted from the sender.

edits.description: When the cloud model has an incident, Happy today answers with a raw error or not at all. With this, a smaller model from the same vendor answers that turn and says so, each parent gets one plain 'the model is down' line and later a 'back' line, and the alerts that need no model (the weather watch, the stop phrase, fixed reminders that must not be missed) keep working.
edits.how:
Today each person agent is generated with `model.fallbacks: []`, and the docs say an agent's primary is strict unless its model object lists fallbacks, so after the built-in retries a failure surfaces as a terminal error that keeps the provider's HTTP status. Three steps. (1) Fallback: add gpt-6-luna on the same per-person provider id as the single fallback for

-main, one line in gen-family, since both models are already in that agent's modelPolicy.allow under the same key and store setting. The docs say a fallback is used for that turn only and a one-line notice is shown in direct chats. Mail and kid agents keep `fallbacks: []` as the roadmap requires. This covers model-scoped incidents and rate limits, not a vendor-wide outage. (2) Model-free jobs: the weather watch (F018) is specified as a `--command-argv` job and the stop phrase (G005) is a `before_dispatch` claim, so both work through an outage. Timed reminders (F007) and the briefs are `--message` jobs, which the docs define as model-backed agent turns, so they fail with the model; a fixed-text reminder that must not be missed, such as bin day, has to be created as a command job that prints its line. A scheduled agent turn can also carry its own `--fallbacks` list. (3) Outage notice: extend the health watch (G008) so that when the existing error-ratio alert has fired for N minutes, a host script sends each parent one fixed line and later one 'back' line by a model-free send: `openclaw message send` to the pinned family handles, or a command job with announce delivery. The catalog's usual host path, `openclaw agent --deliver`, runs an agent turn and so cannot announce a model outage. `openclaw models status --check` is not the detector: its own docs say a clean exit does not prove a request will succeed.
caveats: OpenAI's status history listed 39 incidents in September 2026 and 23 in the first ten days of October across all its products. Most do not touch the API models Happy uses, but some did, for example 'elevated error rates across API models' on 17 Sep.
An answer from the smaller model can be worse than the usual one; the fallback notice tells the parent which model answered.
No fallback to a second vendor: it would need another vendor's key and a new privacy decision, and the local route is the skipped M2, so a vendor-wide outage still means no answers until it ends.
An API key that hits its monthly cap looks like an outage until the month ends; the fixed line should say 'limit reached' when that is the cause.
If the Mac, the home internet or iMessage is what failed, nothing here helps. The dead-man alert is then the only signal and it goes to Tony.
A scheduled brief that fails is simply missed unless the job's retry settings say otherwise.
